clue.text: Without delay when bowler, say, reached the ground

definitions.text: when bowler, say, reached the ground
definitions.meaning: read literally: the moment a hat such as a bowler fell to the floor

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes how quickly a bowler hit the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' wants to be a cricketer; here it is a bowler hat, and a dropped hat was once a starting signal, the literal origin of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately, without needing any persuasion or notice.

clue.text: Bill's relation

definitions.meaning: a bill or invoice for goods or services
a relation is a narrative or report of events

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a family member of a man named Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill's' looks like a man's name with a possessive; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab owed is one sense and a told story or report is another, both meanings of the same word.

clue.text: Walk, parking vehicle first

indicators.note: first says the vehicle comes ahead of the parking letter in the answer

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails in the street
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A driver parks the car before setting off on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge a long way on foot is a synonym of walking.

clue.text: Emigrant has no right to speak at length

indicators.note: has no says a letter is missing from the emigrant word

parts.note: an expatriate is someone living away from their homeland

explanation.surface: An emigrant without rights is still allowed to make long speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound on a subject in detail is a synonym of speaking at length.

clue.text: Right time of life for fashion

parts.note: age is how far through life one is

explanation.surface: Someone says it is the right age to start following trends.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze or current vogue is a sense of fashion.

clue.text: Go on raising a shout of disapproval in game

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the word, reading it from the bottom up

parts.note: keep means go on, continue
boo is a shout of disapproval

explanation.surface: Someone keeps jeering during a sports match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns KEEP into PEEK, read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hiding-and-revealing nursery game played with babies.

clue.text: Embraced by a man, one becomes aroused

indicators.note: embraced by puts the letter for one inside the man's name

parts.note: Fred is a man's name
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by a man becomes excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Fired up means excited or stirred, so the past participle stands for aroused.

clue.text: Settle by discussion what to do with bad tooth

definitions.meaning: to resolve a quarrel by talking it through frankly

definitions.text: what to do with bad tooth
definitions.meaning: read literally, a rotten tooth is best extracted

explanation.surface: Advice on dealing with a dental problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to thrash out a dispute openly; literally it describes pulling out a decayed molar.

clue.text: This figure is not male? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the preceding words are set out incorrectly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone queries whether a statue is not male and decides that is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface denial is itself the joke: the figure is indeed male, a carved man used as a column.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture it is a sculpted male statue serving as a pillar, the male counterpart of a caryatid.

clue.text: Pretend to be in agony, say, to get wine

indicators.note: say tells you the phrase is spoken and the answer only matches its sound

parts.note: sham means pretend, pain means agony, giving a phrase sham pain

explanation.surface: Someone fakes suffering in order to be given a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The French sparkling drink is a type of wine.

clue.text: Composer's party line

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the composer

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: A composer's political party line.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, writer of Boléro.

clue.text: Ruth, first out of bed, is self-important

indicators.note: first says the out-of-bed word is placed ahead of the other

parts.note: up means risen, out of bed
ruth is an old word for compassion, pity

explanation.surface: Ruth, the first to get up, is full of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name; it is the archaic noun for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant and putting on airs is a synonym of self-important.

clue.text: My dad's in disarray, thinking excessively about appearance

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A father is untidy and vain about his looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a dandy is excessive concern with one's dress and looks.

clue.text: Wielder of hammer needing American tool to make chest

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god whose weapon is a hammer
ax is the US spelling of axe

explanation.surface: A hammer-thrower needs an axe to build a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the anatomical term for the chest region of the body.

clue.text: In succession to throne, making changes over time

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the jumbled letters above the time letter
making changes says the letters of these words are reordered

explanation.surface: An heir to the throne reforms things over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means one after another, consecutively.

clue.text: With funny play not finishing its run, have to make a decision

indicators.note: not finishing its run says the play word loses its final letter

parts.note: a comedy is a funny play
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A comedy closed before its run ended, forcing a decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finishing its run' cuts the Y from COMEDY, leaving COMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To come down on one side is to decide in its favour.

clue.text: Disgusting river, with another river within about 200 yards

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England

indicators.note: within puts the second river letter inside the length word

parts.note: a cable is a nautical length of a tenth of a mile, roughly 200 yards
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A foul river with a second stream running into it a short distance away.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominably bad or detestable is a synonym of disgusting.

clue.text: Girl confined — following this youth, perhaps

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman
pent means shut in, confined

explanation.surface: A girl locked away after a wayward youth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the answer is a word that 'youth' often follows, as in the phrase about a wasted adolescence.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is the sense, and the set phrase pairs it with youth.

clue.text: Derisory way to call back

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: back says the call word is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness

explanation.surface: A feeble method for returning a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughably inadequate is a synonym of derisory.

clue.text: Saw person convincingly demonstrating book

parts.note: a prover is one who proves

explanation.surface: Someone showing a book's argument convincingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying, a synonym of a wise maxim.

clue.text: Write a little more than quartet

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tad is a little

explanation.surface: Advice to compose something slightly longer than a piece for four.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a group of five, which is one more than four.

clue.text: Does try to move nothing in crush

indicators.note: to move says one letter of the words before it is shifted to a new place among them

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to shift nothing in a crowded crush.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the O ('nothing') in DOES TRY from second place to sixth and the letters read as the answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush utterly is a synonym of wreck or annihilate.

clue.text: After session of play, players become gloomy

indicators.note: after places the players word following the session word

parts.note: an over is a session of six balls in cricket
a cast is the players in a play

explanation.surface: Cricketers turn glum after a spell of play.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cloud over, darken.

clue.text: Royal companion taking part in Bacchic orgies

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A palace companion joins in a drunken revel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen's pet dogs were famously of this Welsh breed.

clue.text: Golly in bits

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at something broken to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an exclamation of surprise and the plural of tiny food fragments.

clue.text: Design provided after check on vehicle

indicators.note: after places the provided word following the check word

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test on a vehicle
if means provided

explanation.surface: A pattern approved once the car passes inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeated decorative element is a synonym of a design.

clue.text: Students had outstanding exams, getting firsts in Oxford, say

indicators.note: getting firsts says take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Students did brilliantly in exams and got first-class degrees at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university; it is a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of laced leather footwear.

clue.text: In panic, lose head and slip

indicators.note: lose head says the word drops its first letter

parts.note: terror is panic

explanation.surface: Someone panics, loses composure and makes a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a mistake, a synonym of blunder.

clue.text: Hire box — it is arranged for somebody at the show

indicators.note: arranged says these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone hires a box at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: One who displays work at a show is a person at the show.

clue.text: Crazy problem for parish council

definitions.meaning: read literally: flying mammals roosting in the church tower

explanation.surface: Something mad troubling a village church committee.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mad; literally it is roosting animals in the church tower.
